title: Part Thirty: ICE and the Data Stack

sections.brief: ICE's contracts by layer, listed not summed, with date and administration: Palantir (link ow9_ice, de27), LexisNexis Accurint and the Aug 2026 bridge requiring APIs to the Palantir platform, Thomson Reuters CLEAR and LEIDS-5 (TR: Palantir not a CLEAR customer), Babel Street 2018/2019, Penlink Tangles/Webloc $2.3m (ICE did not buy Cobwebs), ShadowDragon 2020/2021, Zignal $5.7m, Cellebrite, Clearview, Paragon (closed Jan 2026); budget link us6_asylum; If it were connected. Figures: money

Third-party doctrine, Carpenter, Chatrie (link ow9_ice, de25); CAI and the ICE/FBI positions; ODNI 2022 report declassified 12 Jun 2023; OIG-23-61; Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act (House 219-199, died), Davidson 2026 amendment, 702 lapse (us10); Montana SB 282; DHS administrative subpoenas (Thomas-Johnson, Instagram six, Philadelphia Doe), EFF letter 10 Feb 2026; USCIS and State vetting; AAUP v. Rubio (Hatch testimony, 30 Sep 2025, Jan 2026 vacatur, appeal pending); If it were connected. Figures: flow

Master diagram: six layers (government records; government-run surveillance; state and local; commercial vendors; data brokers; integration platforms incl. RAVEn) with every node graded documented / probable / reported / possible / not supported; walk-through of the chain; congressional letters (Warner-Kaine and OIG audit, 70 members, Goldman-Velázquez-Wyden 14 Apr 2026, no reply); worst-case reading tested for Part 28.
